Donna di 55 anni con perdite ematiche va: 55-year-old woman with vaginal bleeding. Biopsy of a cervical lesion: squamous cell carcinoma. MRI for local staging (available sequences: large-field axial T2 from the upper abdomen to the pelvis, sagittal T2, oblique coronal and high-resolution axial).
Referta in ordine: tumore, estensione lo: Report in order: tumor, local extent and urinary tract, conclusion.
Il carcinoma squamoso della cervice è qu:
Squamous cell carcinoma of the cervix is almost always linked to persistent infection with high-risk HPV (WHO 2020: HPV-associated tumors, the vast majority, and HPV-independent tumors, which are rare).
In FIGO staging, hydronephrosis or a non-functioning kidney caused by the tumor raises the stage to IIIB, regardless of tumor size (unless another cause is known). For this reason, staging MRI must include a large-field sequence reaching the kidneys: if only the pelvis is examined, hydronephrosis is missed and the stage remains underestimated.
The point where the ureter is interrupted indicates the lateral extent of the tumor toward the pelvic wall. Hydronephrosis should be flagged as urgent: a nephrostomy or stent may be needed before chemoradiotherapy, also to protect renal function during cisplatin.
FIGO 2009 (used in TCGA): IIIA lower third of the vagina; IIIB pelvic wall or hydronephrosis. FIGO 2018 adds IIIC (pelvic lymph nodes IIIC1, para-aortic IIIC2).
Carcinoma della cervice: guarda sempre i: Cervical carcinoma: always look at the kidneys. Tumor-related hydronephrosis = FIGO IIIB.
Carcinoma squamoso della cervice G2, sta: Squamous cell carcinoma of the cervix G2, FIGO stage IIIB (FIGO 2009; TCGA clinical data from the TCGA-CESC collection). The patient's HPV genotype is not available in the public data.
